questions.q: Which chapters' techniques were actually used to diagnose and fix the Meridian Outfitters problem, per this lesson's recap?
options: Only Chapter 8's configuration tuning
Chapter 1 (the loop), Chapter 2 (execution plans), Chapter 3 (covering indexes), and Chapter 5 (wait stats)
Only Chapter 7's Query Store
Every chapter's technique was applied equally
questions.explain: The loop structured the process, plan-reading and wait stats found the cause, and covering-index design supplied the fix — the other chapters' tools weren't the ones this specific bottleneck needed.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does knowing that Chapters 4, 6, 7, and 8's tools did NOT apply here matter?
options: Because a real diagnosis should apply every available technique regardless of relevance
Because those tools are outdated and no longer used in practice
Because ruling out fixes that wouldn't have helped is itself part of a real diagnosis, not wasted effort
Because those chapters are less important than the others
questions.explain: A real diagnosis narrows to the one bottleneck that matters and doesn't reach for MAXDOP or a query rewrite just because those tools exist.

questions.q: What shape does this lesson recommend for turning the capstone into an interview answer?
options: Symptom, root cause, change, and verified result — showing how you knew which fix and how you knew it worked
A list of every DMV name covered in the course
A live demo of unrelated SQL Server features
Just stating that an index was added and it got faster
questions.explain: That structure demonstrates the full loop, not just a fix — which is what distinguishes a strong performance-tuning answer from a vague one.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which three courses join SQL Server Performance Tuning in the Advanced stage of the SQL Server Database Administrator path?
options: Data Science, Data Engineering, and Data Analytics
Salesforce Administration, Salesforce Solutions Architect, and Blockchain Development
T-SQL for Database Administrators, Advanced Excel, and Tableau
SQL Server High Availability, Backup & Disaster Recovery; Azure Database Administrator; and PowerShell Automation & DevOps for DBAs
questions.explain: These four courses make up the Advanced stage of the SQL Server Database Administrator path, alongside the Job-Ready stage completed earlier in the path.

questions.q: Is there a required order among the four Advanced-stage courses, per this lesson?
options: Yes — Azure Database Administrator is a strict prerequisite for the other three
Yes — they must be taken in alphabetical order
Yes — Performance Tuning must always be taken last
No — each covers a different advanced responsibility, and none assumes the others are taken first
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states there's no required order among the four Advanced-stage courses.
